jobs.description:
What to Expect

As a Vehicle Technician with our Attributes team you will play a critical role in the development of Tesla’s industry-leading products. You will help bring the electric vehicle and energy storage products we design to life, and ensure their acoustic integrity. You will work side-by-side with fellow NVH and Vehicle Dynamics staff and other engineering teams to solve the toughest challenges in the industry and deliver world-class performance. Tesla is looking only for the best and most talented. Accelerate your career. Accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy and transport. Role is based in BTEC (Berlin - Germany). Occasional travel is required.

What You’ll Do

- Work independently or alongside other technicians to complete vehicle retrofits and adaptations for attributes performance evaluation 
- Perform and streamline component swaps (tires, springs, stabilizer bars, dampers, bushings, etc.) during NVH and Vehicle Dynamics tuning or evaluation sessions 
- Contribute to fabrication of prototype parts and/or vehicles for engineering development 
- Installation of data acquisition equipment to include sensors (i.e. accelerometers, microphones, gyros, thermocouples, strain gauges, load cells, pressure transducers, torque sensors, displacement sensors, CAN bus traffic, GPS, etc.) 
- Assess vehicle performance for NVH – squeak  and rattle, brake noise, drive unit noise, road and wind noise, HVAC noise. Record test data if required. 
- Maintain Attributes fleet vehicles in excellent condition 
- Maintain test equipment 
- What You’ll Bring
- 3+ years experience working in an automotive dealership, workshop or lab.  
- Strong communication skills, independent worker, and an excellent team player able to work on flexible schedule 
- Excellent knowledge of vehicle and vehicle subsystems operation; knowledge of electric vehicle architecture a strong plus 
- Ability to work independently or as part of a team as needs require, under pressure and adapt to changing priorities 
- Excellent attention to detail and hands on approach 
- Basic understanding of NVH and Vehicle Dynamics, vehicle instrumentation (Siemens and Head Acoustics desirable), CAN communication, and vehicle software 
- Must have a valid driver’s license 
- Language preferences: English and German

About us

At Life Couriers, we understand how important the critical moments in life are.

As the global leader in radiopharmaceutical and stem cell logistics, we have leveraged our experience with some of the world’s most time-critical shipments to expand our services to biopharmaceuticals, cell and gene therapies, laboratory specimens, clinical trials, organ transplants, medical devices, and more.

Because we know that a missed delivery can mean the loss of a life. That is why we have built our company culture around one clear priority: patient outcomes. Our employees are committed to improving, enriching, and saving lives through the power of logistics.

To strengthen our Controlling team, we are looking for a FP&A Controller (m/f/d) to join us as soon as possible.

Your Responsibilities

- Drive monthly management reporting, business reviews and performance analyses for assigned business units
- Partner with business unit heads as a finance sparring partner, providing financial insights, challenging assumptions and supporting operational and strategic decision-making
- Support budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning processes, including the development and maintenance of financial models
- Analyze business performance and variances, identify key business drivers and translate financial data into actionable recommendations
- Support strategic finance initiatives, including commercial improvement, operational optimization, investment decisions and growth opportunities
- Develop and standardize reporting structures, KPIs and planning processes
- Ensure data quality through validation, reconciliation and continuous improvement of reporting processes
- Build and improve scalable FP&A and controlling processes to support the company’s next stage of growth

Your Profile

- Bachelor’s or master’s degree in finance, business administration, economics, business analytics or a comparable field
- First professional experience in FP&A, controlling, finance, audit, transaction services, consulting or business intelligence
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear and concise business insights
- Advanced Excel skills; experience with Power BI or other BI tools highly advantageous; knowledge of LucaNet or Business Central a plus
- Proactive, structured and independent working style with a hands-on mentality, strong ownership and attention to details
- Confident communication and strong business partnering skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with finance teams, business unit leaders and management in an international environment
- Fluent in German and English, both written and spoken

What We Offer

- A high-impact FP&A role with early responsibility for business unit performance and direct exposure to senior management
- The opportunity to shape finance structures, reporting, and decision-making in a growing and dynamic environment
- The opportunity to leverage and further develop your expertise across business partnering, analytics, strategic finance, transformation topics, and the value creation agenda of a private equity portfolio company
- A collaborative, international team with flat hierarchies, short decision-making paths, and the opportunity to make a visible contribution
- Flexible working model including home office options and flexible working hours (flextime)
- 30 days of annual leave
- Access to employee benefits such as Wellpass or Sodexo
- A purpose-driven company environment, contributing to meaningful healthcare logistics at Life Couriers
- A modern, supportive workplace where your ideas and impact truly matter

Application

Have we sparked your interest? We look forward to receiving your application!

Please send your complete application (CV, cover letter, references), including your salary expectations and earliest possible start date, to: recruiting@lifecouriers.com (https://mailto:recruiting@lifecouriers.com)

We welcome applications from all backgrounds, regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

Help Accelerate Industrial Decarbonization

Join exceptional people from around the world to solve some of the world's toughest energy challenges, make a real impact, and enjoy the adventure of building the future of industrial decarbonization together.

As our Senior Manufacturing & Industrialization Engineer (m/f/d), you will play a key role in turning our proprietary solar-thermal technology into scalable, repeatable production systems that can be deployed around the world.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning two unique manufacturing environments: component production through external manufacturing partners, and the construction of large solar fields as disciplined, measurable production systems. You will take work from early concept and specification through supplier delivery, commissioning, ramp-up and continuous improvement.

Your Impact

Your work will help turn innovative engineering into reliable production and large-scale deployment.

You’ll shape how our technology is manufactured and deployed—from developing production processes and equipment to improving how solar fields are built in the field. Working across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Project Delivery, Construction and HSE, you’ll help create safer, more efficient and repeatable ways of delivering our technology at scale.

What You'll Do

Lead Manufacturing & Industrialization

- Lead manufacturing and industrialization strategy for assigned products, component families and solar-field work packages.
- Own complex equipment and industrialization programmes, including technical scope, interfaces, risk, schedule, investment and acceptance.
- Provide technical leadership, coaching and task direction to engineers and other contributors, helping build GlassPoint's manufacturing-engineering capability.
- Lead cross-functional reviews and present clear process-selection, investment and risk recommendations to senior stakeholders.

Develop Production Systems & Equipment

- Develop manufacturing processes, machine concepts and equipment specifications for GlassPoint's proprietary concentrating mirrors and film panels.
- Help turn solar-field construction into a repeatable field-production system with defined workflows, work packages, tooling, crew structures and productivity measures.
- Develop or specify production equipment, tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges and handling solutions suited to factories and remote sites.
- Work with external equipment builders, integrators and manufacturing partners through technical evaluation, design review, FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up.

Improve Performance & Scale

- Apply DFMA, process capability, standard work, line balancing, cycle-time and capacity analysis to improve safety, quality, output and cost.
- Choose the right level of automation—from simple manual aids through mechanised tooling to automated equipment—based on volume, workforce capability, maintainability and economics.
- Work across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Project Delivery, Construction and HSE, capturing lessons and improving each subsequent deployment.

Who You Are

- You're someone who enjoys solving complex manufacturing challenges and turning ambitious technology into practical, scalable production.
- You know the best solution isn't always the most automated one and can balance quality, safety, cost and output with maintainability and simplicity.
- You enjoy working hands-on with engineering teams, suppliers and manufacturing partners, and are comfortable travelling internationally, including to remote project locations and for extended visits during commissioning and ramp-up.
- Most importantly, you're excited to influence both the product and how it is manufactured and deployed at scale.

Ideally, you'll bring:

- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Production Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- Typically 10+ years of relevant manufacturing or industrialisation experience, with direct responsibility for production processes, equipment or line deployment.
- A strong record of specifying, procuring, commissioning and ramping production machinery, tooling or automated/semi-automated systems.
- Experience leading engineers, project teams or technical workstreams; formal people-management experience is desirable.
- Deep practical knowledge of DFMA, process capability, tolerancing, error-proofing, line balancing, standard work and continuous improvement.
- Confidence working with equipment builders, system integrators and outsourced manufacturers, including FAT and SAT.
- Experience with large assemblies, modular systems, construction operations or field-deployed production is highly desirable.
- Practical, commercially aware and comfortable making structured decisions with incomplete information.
- Strong English communication skills and willingness to travel internationally, sometimes for extended project phases.

What You'll Find at GlassPoint

- Real ownership and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact from day one.
- Exceptional colleagues from diverse disciplines who challenge, support, and learn from each other.
- Complex challenges that require curiosity, collaboration, and innovation.
- An international team united by a shared purpose and ambitious goals.
- The adventure of helping build the future of industrial decarbonization.

We value inclusion and foster a culture of belonging, welcoming team members of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, gender identity, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. We have zero tolerance for discrimination, harassment, bullying, or retaliation.

GlassPoint helps heavy industry decarbonize by replacing fuel-based steam with solar thermal heat. This reduces energy costs and improves long-term energy security. We’re a proven technology, already operating some of the world’s largest solar steam projects across sun-belt regions in oil and gas, metals, and mining.

For our Berlin office, we are seeking a versatile and committed

Communications Student Assistant

to join its team in Berlin as soon as possible for initially twelve months, with possibility of renewal, and with a weekly average workload of 19.5 hours. The hourly remuneration is in accordance with the Tarifvertrag für studentische Beschäftigte (TV Stud III), Berlin.

Regular support of ALLEA’s communications activities:

- Support in establishing and maintaining media contact databases, creating stakeholder outreach lists, and designing strategies to communicate ALLEA’s work.
- Assist the communications team in drafting website posts and press releases, and in the day-to-day management of social media channels and blog
- Help prepare, edit, proofread, and layout ALLEA newsletters, publications, leaflets, etc.
- Support the team with preparation, execution, and follow-up of digital, hybrid or in-person public events as well as working group and committee meetings.
- Media monitoring, project administration and general office tasks are also part of this role.

What we are looking for:

- Be a graduate student enrolled in a university programme for at least 12 months after starting the ALLEA position, preferably in a communications-related field (communications or media studies, journalism, marketing, etc.), or in other social science fields (international relations, sociology, political science, etc.) with a strong interest in communications.

- Have very good organisational skills, hands-on approach, and a keen eye for detail; ability to work independently and in a team; flexibility with regards to working in an office setting or remotely as needed.
- Have an interest in ALLEA’s areas of expertise (international relations, public policy, scientific collaboration, science communications, research policy, scientific advice to policymaking, etc.) 

What we offer: 

- International working environment as part of a committed team with flat hierarchies.
- Options to work flexibly between our office facilities in the centre of Berlin and remotely.
- Employment contract follows regulations of German TV-L collective agreement, overtime compensation, and 31 annual leave days on a 5-day week base (including 24 and 31 December).
- Job ticket subsidy of 40 Euro per month (Deutschlandticket) and company pension scheme subsidy (bAV).

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

In close collaboration with your team, you will play a key role within the global insurance and risk management of Siemens Energy. Working closely with your team, brokers, and insurers, you will actively shape the placement of corporate liability and financial lines insurance programs in the international insurance market, provide advisory support to business units on complex contracts, and manage challenging claims. Your daily responsibilities will integrate legal and insurance expertise, strategic business thinking, negotiation skills, and the ability to effectively communicate complex issues.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Responsibility for the design, placement, implementation, and management of corporate liability and financial lines insurance programs, including the development of insurance terms and coverage concepts, considering the needs and risk profile of our business units
* Advising and placing liability project insurance
* Primary contact for insurance-related questions regarding contract structures and active participation in contract negotiations worldwide
* Supporting business units in reporting and processing insurance claims, as well as analysing and evaluating insurance solutions. Independently handling complex claims, with a particular focus on operational, product, and environmental liability claims, and managing claims processes abroad
* First point of contact for senior management-related questions regarding insurance coverage for the board and management in accordance with German corporate law

What You Bring

* Several years of relevant professional experience in a comparable position or relevant industry experience, particularly in the placement of international insurance programs, contract commentary, and claims handling in international project business
* Fluent in German (C1/C2) and English (C1), both written and spoken. Additional language skills, such as Spanish, are desirable
* Analytical skills and a confident approach to complex issues, connecting legal, technical, and economic aspects into clear recommendations
* Confident in negotiations, high level of personal responsibility, structured working style, and enjoyment of proactive topic advancement
* Proficient in all common MS Office applications and generative AI, with an affinity for implementing digital processes

About the Team

In our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more.

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.

What you will do

- Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
- Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
- Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.
- Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.
- Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.
- Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.
- Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.
- Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.

What we are looking for

- Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.
- Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.
- Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance.
- Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more.
- Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows.
- Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership.
- Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty.
- Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries.

Useful experience, but not required

- DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems.
- Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems.
- GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
- Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing.
- Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations.
- Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby.

What we offer you

At Smartly, we offer a place where you can do meaningful technical work while growing with a global team.

- Inclusive global culture built on trust, transparency, open feedback, and respect for different perspectives.
- Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale.
- Wellbeing support, paid holidays, family leave, and sustainable ways of working.
- Equity options, performance-based rewards, competitive compensation, and career development opportunities.
- A flexible hybrid workplace that balances office collaboration with focused remote work. At Smartly we work 3 days a week from the office.

About Smartly

Smartly is an advertising technology company helping brands create, manage, optimize, and understand digital advertising across major media platforms. Our engineering organization builds the systems that connect media, creative, and intelligence capabilities into a product used by customers globally.

We value clear communication, ownership, curiosity, and collaboration across teams. We want Smartly to be a place where people can do strong work, grow, and feel respected.

Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, ownership, curiosity, and the ability to build reliable systems with others. Direct experience with every technology listed here is less important than the judgment to learn, reason from first principles, and ship useful platform capabilities.

About Smartly

Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers.

Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. jobs.description:
Would you like to own driving revenue and customer engagements for a leader in the Cloud Computing business? Would you like to be part of a team focused on increasing awareness and adoption of Amazon Web Services by engaging with Public Sector organizations in Germany who are reinventing their IT strategy by adopting cloud computing? Do you have the business savvy, sales experience, and technical background necessary to help further establish Amazon as a leading cloud platform provider?

As a Greenfield Account Executive within Amazon Web Services (AWS) Worldwide Public Sector (WWPS), you will build AWS adoption in net-new public sector accounts with limited or no existing AWS presence. You will own the full sales cycle, from prospecting through close, helping public sector organizations reinvent their IT strategy through cloud computing.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in full sales cycle, technology sales, sales engineering/consulting or equivalent business development
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience
- Experience using sales CRM tools such as Salesforce
- Fluent in German and English with the ability to conduct sales and technical conversations with customers in both languages
- Experience developing and executing sales strategies, tactics, plans, processes, systems and programs
- Experience in generating new opportunities with strong focus on pipeline tracking and deal execution through entire sales cycle

Preferred qualifications

- AWS Associate level certification, or Bachelor's degree in business administration, finance, economics, computer science, data science, engineering, or other related field
- Experience with government procurement and contracting process
- Experience working with partners through account, product or program management and business development engagements
- Experience selling nascent products and services Ability to drive solutions to difficult problems
- Experience driving new business in greenfield accounts at the C-suite level or equivalent
- Experience in strategic thinking about business, enterprise software products, and new technology platforms and architectures or equivalent

This role requires building a sales function from the ground up, demanding creative problem-solving, tenacity, and the ability to develop novel approaches for reaching and engaging prospective customers. You will establish business and technical relationships with public sector organizations, driving adoption of AWS services that transform how they deliver services to citizens and communities.

You will engage customers face-to-face and via teleconference, interacting at the CXO level in strategic accounts. The ideal candidate possesses both business acumen to drive executive-level engagements and technical knowledge to interact effectively with software developers and architects.

This position requires working from the local office when not at customer sites.

Key job responsibilities
Sales Execution
• Prospect and qualify net-new public sector accounts with limited or no AWS presence
• Manage the full sales cycle from prospecting through close
• Meet or exceed quarterly revenue targets while maintaining robust pipeline coverage
• Maintain accurate sales forecasts and pipeline reporting in Salesforce

Customer Engagement
• Develop and execute territory plans to maximize market penetration
• Translate cloud and AI capabilities into mission-relevant use cases for public sector organizations
• Build relationships across customer organizations, including C-level executives, engineering, IT/operations, and procurement
• Conduct discovery calls to understand agency missions and technical challenges

Public Sector Expertise
• Navigate public sector procurement processes including RFPs, cooperative contracts, and federal/state/local contract vehicles
• Apply knowledge of public sector compliance requirements, certifications, and fiscal year buying cycles
• Structure deals that meet public sector regulatory, compliance, and grant-funded operating requirements

Collaboration
• Partner with solutions architects and internal stakeholders to accelerate deal velocity
• Collaborate with the partner ecosystem (systems integrators, resellers, distributors) to drive customer success and extend market reach
• Use data and insights to prioritize outreach and identify high-potential prospects

A day in the life
You will balance hunting new accounts with nurturing early-stage relationships. Working with a team of German AE's to grow the Public Sector Greenfield business. You will spend time on prospecting, researching accounts, sourcing contacts, and executing outbound campaigns to generate meetings. jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is growing rapidly, and we are looking for a Data Center Operations Manager to join our expanding Infrastructure Operations team in our site in Berlin.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

We are currently expanding our infrastructure management team and we are looking for a manager with experience in people leadership, a strong technical understanding of data center operations and infrastructure, and the drive and vision to take AWS Data Center Operations into the future.

The Data Center Manager is the leadership role for our compute operations teams within an AWS region. They will have managerial responsibility for safety, security, availability, scaling, costs and efficiency for their department. They lead the team that is installing, maintaining, and de-commissioning network and server equipment in a safe, secure and cost-effective manner across the region. The Data Center Operations Manager must manage across each function but also have the ability to dive deep into any given function as needed.

Key job responsibilities
Lead and supervise a team of Data Center Technicians which is installing, maintaining and decommissioning network and server hardware

- Oversee the safety, security, availability, quality, and performance of the team, while driving a positive customer experience
- Strategic planning and forecasting; manage team and individual performance; delivering performance reviews, and address staffing needs
- Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and procedures
- Mentor, train and develop career progression for direct reports and members of the organization
- Coordinate the shift work among the team and ensure 24 hours coverage available for our data centers
- Maintant on-call duties
- Obsess over team learning and development, both from a technical/functional and soft skills (critical thinking, emotional intelligence, and adaptability) development perspective
- Coordinate support of change management resources in partnership with electrical and mechanical operations teams
- Develop, improve, and share operational best practices across the region and with peers globally
